request.spec:
For bigger amounts put commas in. Show it like $1,234.50. Do this everywhere an amount shows,
including on the invoices and on the client statement.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read CLAUDE.md — it states the working rules, the project layout, and the data-testid
conventions. Follow it.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
For bigger amounts put commas in. Show it like $1,234.50. Do this everywhere an amount shows,
including on the invoices and on the client statement.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, and any audit records it
expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as you work;
iterate until it passes. Implement the full-stack change (database migration + OfficeFloor
server + front-end). Do NOT edit the pinned scaffolding (bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop,
bin/e2e, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md) or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Test passes.

The change was a single-point fix. Every money figure in the app — invoice amounts, line items, payments, dashboard totals, and the client statement — already routes through the shared `formatMoney` helper in `ui/money.ts`. Updating that one helper from `.toFixed(2)` to `.toLocaleString('en-US', { minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 })` adds thousands separators everywhere amounts show, so `1234.5` now renders as `$1,234.50`.

No schema or server change was needed: amounts are stored and served as numbers; thousands separators are purely a display concern, and the fix stays composed in the canonical formatter rather than branched per feature. The e2e test passes.
